text:
maria-sales: Hey team — Acadia Health POC kickoff. They want Redwood Private deployed into their AWS account (spoke VPC) but egress must go through their on‑prem proxy (TLS inspect) and they need original client IPs in our request logs for audit. Also security wants a small allowlist of static egress IPs to add to their firewall. Any constraints or config snippets we should hand them?

raj-netops: short answer: we can do the POC but preserving original client IP end‑to‑end is tricky if there's a proxy doing SNAT/TLS inspect. Two patterns: 1) PrivateLink / interface endpoint to our VPC/connector — customer traffic originates from their app IPs -> endpoint ENIs and reaches our connector; if their on‑prem proxy sits upstream of the app, the proxy will SNAT and we only see proxy IPs. 2) If they want true client IP in logs, they need to forward X‑Forwarded‑For from the proxy and not SNAT, or use a TCP passthrough that preserves SKIP-SNI-inspect path.

sam-se: @raj-netops can you spell out what firewall rules they need on their side for PrivateLink + onprem egress?

raj-netops: Sure — high level: allow outbound to our endpoint's IPs (if using interface endpoints) or allow inbound from our connector CIDR if we create an endpoint service. Typical rules:
```
# On customer firewall / proxy
allow tcp 443 from <app-subnet-cidr> to <privatelink-endpoint-ip>/32
allow tcp 443 from <proxy-ip> to 0.0.0.0/0 (if proxy does egress to internet)
# If we host connector in their VPC (recommended for POC):
allow tcp 443 from their app subnets to connector ENI security group
```
Also, if they need static egress IPs for calls to external services (not Redwood), that is on their NAT egress. For our handoff they only need to allow traffic to our endpoint/service IPs.

jess-ps: Security requested a concrete small allowlist for the vendor team. Can we give them a minimal set they can paste into their firewall ticket?

raj-netops: We can give two variants depending on topology:
- If we use AWS Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) into Redwood-hosted connector: give the endpoint ENI IPs (AWS assigns) — those are per-AZ and might change on re-create. Not ideal for a static allowlist.
- If we deploy a connector VM in their VPC (recommended POC), we can allocate Elastic IPs on NAT Gateway/ALB and provide 2 static EIPs for HA. Those are stable and easy to allowlist.

Suggested allowlist snippet for connector-in-VPC option:
```
# Allowlist on customer edge firewall
203.0.113.12/32  # Connector EIP A (outbound from apps to connector via NAT/ALB)
203.0.113.13/32  # Connector EIP B
# Ports
TCP 443 (HTTPS) both directions as needed
ICMP allowed between monitoring hosts (optional)
```

maria-sales: That sounds good. What about ports for health checks and observability? They run strict egress rules.

raj-netops: Health check URLs use HTTPS 443 by default. If we add metrics scraping, we generally use port 9100 or 9102 but for the POC keep everything over 443 to avoid extra rules. If they need Prometheus scraping from their monitoring to connector, we can expose a metrics endpoint bound to localhost and proxy over a TLS port — but again, simplest is 443.

sam-se: Pricing note from Acadia: they asked whether PrivateLink vs deploying our connector in their VPC affects cost. Any quick line I can send to procurement?

jess-ps: Quick summary: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) has AWS data processing charges + normal network usage; deploying connector in-customer VPC means customer pays the connector infra (EC2/EIP/NAT) and Redwood charges a Private deployment platform fee (POC discounts possible). For POC we usually offer a temporary credit for infra so they only see minimal cloud charges. I'll follow up with finance for exact numbers.

maria-sales: Security questionnaire: they want confirmation that TLS is terminated only on our connector and that we support customer‑managed KMS for keys. Also auditing requirements: can we emit request IDs and integrate with their SIEM via syslog?

raj-netops: TLS: if the customer requires TLS inspection on their side, they can front the client->connector traffic with their proxy — but Redwood will still validate upstream TLS to origins when making outbound calls. For end‑to‑end mutual TLS we support client cert validation at the connector. KMS: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations for at‑rest encryption of model artifacts and logs (we'll provide config keys). Auditing: we can emit request metadata including request IDs and X‑Forwarded‑For if provided; for SIEM integration we can forward logs via TLS syslog to a customer endpoint or ship to their S3 bucket (signed).

deploy-bot: Created temporary POC connector cluster in acct 123456789012 (us-east-1). ID: connector-poc-3345.

sam-se: Nice — can you confirm the connector's expected CIDR and whether we should use EIPs?

raj-netops: Connector cluster sits in 10.45.32.0/22 in the customer's spoke VPC. For stable allowlisting give them two EIPs on the ALB in front of connectors. I'll need network owner to provision and attach.

maria-sales: Next steps / owner list:
- raj-netops: produce final allowlist + short network runbook (1 page) — due EOD tomorrow.
- jess-ps: draft POC pricing line and confirm credits.
- sam-se: fill security questionnaire answers for TLS/KMS/audit and send to Acadia.
- maria-sales: schedule 30m handoff call with customer + netops tomorrow.

raj-netops: I'll include sample iptables/security group rules and an example CIDR mapping for peering vs endpoint setups. Also will note the tradeoffs: PrivateLink = less infra for customer but ephemeral ENI IPs; Connector-in-VPC = stable EIPs and full visibility but customer bears infra.

maria-sales: Perfect. If anyone has short wording for the firewall ticket I can paste, drop it here.

raj-netops: Paste this to firewall ticket: 
"Please allow outbound HTTPS (TCP/443) from app subnet 10.10.0.0/20 to connector EIPs 203.0.113.12 and 203.0.113.13 (for Redwood POC). Allow inbound HTTPS from connector EIPs to app load balancer if using ALB integration. If using PrivateLink endpoint, allow traffic to interface endpoint ENI IPs provided in follow-up."
